title: Invariance of relative simplicial homotopy classes under target equivalence
statement: Use simplicial sets, products, quasicategories, Kan complexes and weak homotopy equivalences from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and categorical equivalences from [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure]. All objects fit in a fixed sufficiently large universe. Let $A\subseteq B$ be a simplicial subset, $u:X\to Y$ a simplicial map, and $a:A\to X$ a simplicial map. Let $[B,X]_a$ denote maps $f:B\to X$ restricting exactly to $a$, modulo the equivalence relation generated by pairs admitting a map $H:B\times\Delta^1\to X$ with those endpoints and $H|_{A\times\Delta^1}=a\circ\operatorname{pr}_1$. Define $[B,Y]_{ua}$ in the same way. In either of the following two cases, postcomposition induces a bijection $u_*:[B,X]_a\xrightarrow{\sim}[B,Y]_{ua}$: (i) $X,Y$ are Kan complexes and $u$ is a weak homotopy equivalence, with no restriction on $A$; (ii) $X,Y$ are quasicategories, $u$ is a categorical equivalence, and $A$ contains every vertex of $B$. Empty extension sets and $A=B$ are allowed.

source.place: HTT Proposition 1.2.7.3(2) and Proposition 1.2.5.3 (equivalences on functor categories and their cores), with the strict-fiber argument for restriction. Restriction is an isofibration by Kerodon Corollary 4.4.5.3 (01F3), and equivalences in a functor category are detected at vertices. For Kan targets the restriction map is a Kan fibration. Apply Kerodon Proposition 3.2.8.1 (00XC) to the restriction square of Kan complexes (cores in case (ii)). The all-vertices condition identifies its strict fiber with the relative diagrams in (ii). These are the precise ingredients of the stated corollary, not a verbatim assertion of one HTT proposition. Read online 2026-10-17; no archived HTT/Kerodon copy in literature/. No Stacks tag states this simplicial homotopy assertion.
